name: dasel-uniform-reader-complexity-budgets
instr:
dasel cannot currently bound resources consumed when direct, CLI, and library reads parse registered formats. Add predictable limits for native parsing work, preserve unlimited results, and return structured, deterministic failures consistently across entry points.

`ReadLimits` independently bounds input bytes, depth, values, documents, scalar bytes, and format-native work. Zero is unlimited; usage is fresh per read. `LimitKind` has exactly `LimitInputBytes = "input-bytes"`, `LimitDepth = "depth"`, `LimitValues = "values"`, `LimitDocuments = "documents"`, `LimitScalarBytes = "scalar-bytes"`, and `LimitFormatWork = "format-work"`. Rejections return no value and a `LimitError` with format, kind, maximum, observed usage, native operation, and any codec error preserved by `LimitError.Unwrap` for `errors.Is`. Input-processing order determines which failure wins when one event crosses multiple budgets.

`Format.NewReader` must snapshot every `ReaderOptions`, pass identical options to custom and built-in constructors, and isolate accounting from mutations and other readers. JSON, YAML, CSV, HCL, TOML, XML, KDL, INI, and dasel readers must meter physical source structures, scalar content, produced model values, and format-native work at native semantic boundaries. Distinguish parser work from decoded model nodes and ignored syntax, including HCL and TOML expressions, blocks, and tables, XML comments, and KDL arguments absent from final values. Enforce common depth and scalar limits.
